title: Onboard build matrix and pin API for heterogeneous expert kernels (MoE/GQA/MHA)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Provide a repeatable build matrix, a lightweight pin API surface, and a published performance-profile format to onboard models with heterogeneous attention/expert patterns (MoE, GQA, grouped-MHA). This ticket scopes the compilation/build variants, profiling matrix, semantic versioning for kernel profiles, and the rollout gating for publishing a profile to the model catalog and runtime pin surface. Deliverables: 1) build matrix document + CI job templates; 2) 'pin' API prototype and server-side validation; 3) profile schema and signed artifact publishing flow; 4) canary rollout automation (5%->25%->100%) with telemetry gates.
decisions: Publish kernel profiles as semantic-tagged artifacts: <model>@<model_version>#kernel-profile:v<major>.<minor>
Pin surface will accept tuples (model, model_version, kernel_profile_tag) and optional rollout_policy string; pinning is reversible with an atomic rollback tag

Profiles include performance buckets for seq lengths [32,128,512], batch sizes [1,8,64], expert_shards [16,64] and recommended compile flags (e.g., fused_kernels=true, int8_packed=false) rather than raw compiler flags to avoid ABI drift

Telemetry gate thresholds: p50 latency regressions <= 2% and token-throughput regression <= 5% compared to baseline for canary to promote; quality regressions (generation LM score / eval prompts) must be <= 0.5% increase in perplexity / regression equivalent
Default routing policy will prefer lower-latency profile for P0 tenants and cost-optimized profile for burst/dedicated-savings groups.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff - aligned with Runtime, Onboarding, and Console PMs. Scoped CI artifacts and profile schema. Assigned small spike to validate MoE sharded-kernel build on A100/MI300 mixtures.

2026-03-11: Spike results - discovered two failure modes at high expert counts: (1) kernel launch serialization on 2D-expert-shard layout, (2) excessive per-expert scratch memory at seq=512. Documented workaround: increase persistent scratch to 1.5x and enable expert-batch coalescing in runtime for 16->64 shards.

2026-03-12: Implemented initial pin API endpoint prototype (POST /pins) + validation middleware. Basic checks: profile checksum, model_version exists, compile-tag signature present. Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1246.

2026-03-13: Telemetry harness completed for seq=[32,128,512] and batch=[1,8,64] on infra-qa cluster. Baseline run (reference profile v1.0) established. Observed 3.8% throughput improvement for grouped-MHA with fused-kernels; MoE improvements are workload-dependent.
acceptance_criteria: CI produces deterministic build artifacts for all matrix combos (architecture x seq x batch x expert_shard) and stores checksums in artifact registry
Pin API accepts profile artifacts and persists an auditable record (actor, timestamp, checksum) visible in Console's rollout page
Profile schema published and validated by server (JSON schema): includes metadata, perf-buckets, recommended runtime flags, and signature
Canary rollout automation exists and will block promotion if telemetry gate thresholds are breached
End-to-end test: onboard one reference GQA model and pin profile v1.1; run canary at 5% traffic and observe telemetry within gates for 24 hours
tests: Microbench harness: runs tokens/sec, p50/p99 latency, GPU memory, and kernel occupancy for seq lengths [32,128,512] and batches [1,8,64]
MoE-specific: expert-hotspot test (skewed routing) with expert_skew=[0.2,0.8] to measure tail latency and per-expert memory amplification
Quality regression: run canonical eval prompts (prompt-set v2026-03) comparing baseline and candidate profile; measure avg logprobs and ROUGE/BLEU where applicable
Stress test: 12h continuous inference with autoscaling boundaries exercised to ensure stable KV cache and no memory leaks under pinned profile
Rollback test: simulate failed canary (force p50 latency +10%) and assert automatic revert to previous profile within 5 minutes
rollout_plan: Publish profile to staging registry -> pin to staging model queue -> run 5% canary for 24h with telemetry gating -> if green, expand to 25% for 12h -> expand to 100% with gradual smoothing. Console shows pin history and allows manual abort. All promotions require signed artifact and CI green badge.
risks: ABI/driver incompatibility across GPU families causing silent perf regressions
Profile explosion: combinatorial growth of profiles (seq x batch x expert_shard x arch) will increase storage/maintenance burden
Quality regressions from aggressive kernel fusion or int8 paths affecting generation distributions
Onboarding friction for model teams due to strict profile validation rules
mitigation: ABI: require CI verification on representative GPUs (A100, H100, MI300) and abort profile publish if checksum mismatches or perf cliffs detected
Profile lifecycle: implement retention/compaction policy (keep last 3 major revisions and best-known-perf per model_version)
Quality: include a lightweight generation-ref test in profile validation and require manual signoff for int8-enabled profiles
Developer UX: provide a one-click helper in Console that generates a recommended profile from a profiling run and drafts the pin request
